Alex (Support): Customer on Vercel edge runtime — streaming chat stalls after ~90s then client sees `401 Unauthorized`, subsequent retries hit `503 Service Unavailable`. They're on node-ts SDK v0.7.2. Request: need repro steps and short-term workaround.
Ellie (Eng): Can you paste the handler snippet and any headers? Is this using the Edge runtime (Vercel) or Node on a server? Also which auth flow — rotating token or short-lived key?
Alex (Support): Edge runtime (Vercel). They rotate tokens from their auth service every 60s. Handler looks like:```ts
export default async function handler(req, ev) {
  const token = await getCurrentToken(); // rotates periodically
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-4o-stream', prompt: '...' })
  });
  // pipe response back to client in edge runtime
  return new Response(res.body, { headers: { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream' } });
}
```
Alex (Support): Customer reports it consistently hangs ~85-95s, then first chunk returns 401 in their client, then retries from their fetch wrapper produce 503s.
Sam (Oncall): Edge keep-alive + auth rotation looks suspicious. If the upstream server sees the connection opened with token A and later token B is issued, any retry that reuses pooled connection might still try token B but some intermediaries reject. Does their SDK do automatic credential refresh mid-stream?
Alex (Support): SDK they used is @redwood/inference v0.7.2 (node). They call the high-level streaming helper which wraps fetch and has built-in retries.
Ellie (Eng): Likely cause: credential provider (getCurrentToken) bound globally, not per-request, and our streaming helper may re-resolve credentials on retry, causing mid-stream rotation semantics. If a connection is still open and a retry triggers a new request with a rotated token, upstream services (or Vercel front) sometimes return 503s for a short window. Short-term workaround: pin a single token for the duration of the stream. Example fix for handler:```ts
const token = await getCurrentToken(); // resolve once
const res = await fetch(url, { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` }, body });
```
and avoid calling getCurrentToken() inside per-chunk callbacks.
Ellie (Eng): Long-term: SDK change to bind credentials per-request and avoid mid-stream re-resolve. I opened INF-3245 for this and attached a small repro harness. Recommend customers upgrade to v0.7.4 (contains credential-binding fix) or apply pinning workaround.
Alex (Support): Can you confirm whether this also triggers billing/usage quirks? Customer said they saw duplicate token usage and unexpected retries billed.
Ellie (Eng): Yes, retries can cause duplicate partial invoiceable tokens if the upstream accepted some tokens then failed mid-stream. We log token IDs in internal traces — will add a regression alert. For now advise customer: use a service token for long streams or upgrade SDK. Also set retries: 1 and increase backoff to avoid flood. Example config:```js
client = new RedwoodClient({ retries: 1, retryBackoffMs: 1000 });
```
CI-Bot: Reproduction job queued: tests/edge-token-rotation-stream.test -> run id: r-20260322-58. Notifying eng-oncall.
Alex (Support): Thanks — I'll reply to customer with the workaround (pin token per stream + set retries low) and the upgrade path v0.7.4. I'll link INF-3245 and ask for a hotfix if the customer is on Dedicated. :thumbsup:
Ellie (Eng): Thanks — I'll add a small note in the release notes and push a patch branch.
Sam (Oncall): If customer is on Dedicated, please open an escalation with infra with the hostnames and we can hot-redeploy a compatible runtime to avoid the 503 window.
Alex (Support): Will do.
